units.literal: King Han and Xiang Yu faced each other across Guangwu and spoke.

units.zh: 羽欲與漢王獨身挑戰，漢王數羽曰：「吾始與羽俱受命懷王，曰先定關中者王之。
units.en: Xiang Yu wanted to challenge the King of Han to single combat. The King of Han instead listed Xiang Yu's crimes: "At first, Xiang Yu and I both received King Huai's command, which said that whoever first pacified Guanzhong would be made king there.
units.literal: Xiang Yu wanted to challenge King Han to single combat. King Han listed Xiang Yu's crimes: "I and Xiang Yu both received commands from King Huai, saying whoever first pacified Guanzhong would be made king.

units.zh: 羽大怒，伏弩射中漢王。
units.en: Xiang Yu was greatly angered and had a crossbow shoot King Han.
units.literal: Xiang Yu was greatly angered and had a crossbow shoot King Han.

units.zh: 漢王傷胸，乃捫足曰：「虜中吾指！」
units.en: King Han was wounded in the chest, but he patted his foot and said: "The bandit hit my toe!"
units.literal: King Han was wounded in the chest, but he patted his foot and said: "The bandit hit my toe!"

units.zh: 漢王病創臥，張良彊請漢王起行勞軍，以安士卒，毋令楚乘勝。
units.en: The King of Han lay ill from his wound. Zhang Liang strongly urged him to get up and go comfort the army, in order to steady the officers and soldiers and not let Chu exploit its victory.
units.literal: King Han lay ill from his wound. Zhang Liang strongly urged King Han to rise and go encourage the troops to stabilize the soldiers and officers, not letting Chu take advantage of their victory.

units.zh: 漢王出行軍，疾甚，因馳入成皋。
units.en: King Han went out to encourage the troops, but his illness was severe, so he galloped into Chenggao.
units.literal: King Han went out to encourage the troops, but his illness was severe, so he galloped into Chenggao.

units.zh: 漢王疾瘉，西入關，至櫟陽，存問父老，置酒。
units.en: King Han recovered from his illness, entered the passes to the west, reached Queyang, visited the elders, and held a banquet.
units.literal: King Han recovered from his illness, entered the passes to the west, reached Queyang, visited the elders, and held a banquet.

units.zh: 漢王怒，欲攻之。
units.en: King Han was angry and wanted to attack him.
units.literal: King Han was angry and wanted to attack him.

units.zh: 漢王下令：軍士不幸死者，吏為衣衾棺斂，轉送其家。
units.en: King Han issued an order: For soldiers who unfortunately die, officials shall provide burial clothes, coffins, and shrouds, and transport them home.
units.literal: King Han issued an order: For soldiers who unfortunately die, officials shall provide burial clothes, coffins, and shrouds, and transport them home.

units.zh: 漢王欲西歸，張良、陳平諫曰：「今漢有天下太半，而諸侯皆附，楚兵罷食盡，此天亡之時，不因其幾而遂取之，所謂養虎自遺患也。」
units.en: The King of Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised him: "Han now possesses more than half the realm, and all the feudal lords have attached themselves to it. Chu's troops are exhausted and its food is gone. This is the moment when Heaven is destroying Chu. If we do not seize this opportunity and take it, that is what is called raising a tiger and leaving disaster for oneself."
units.literal: King Han wanted to return west. Zhang Liang and Chen Ping advised: "Now Han possesses more than half the world, and all the feudal lords are attached. Chu troops are exhausted and food is finished. This is the time Heaven has doomed them. If we do not take advantage of this opportunity to destroy them, this is called raising a tiger that brings disaster to oneself."

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 簡文夜夢吞一塊土，意甚不悅，以告不害，不害曰：「昔晉文公出奔，野人遺之塊，卒反晉國，陛下此夢，事符是乎？」
units.en: Emperor Jianwen one night dreamed he swallowed a clod of earth and was very displeased. He told Buhai, and Buhai said, "In old times Duke Wen of Jin went into exile; a rustic gave him a clod, and in the end he returned to Jin. Your Majesty's dream—does the matter match this?"
units.literal: Emperor Jianwen one night dreamed he swallowed a clod of earth and was very displeased. He told Buhai, and Buhai said: "In old times Duke Wen of Jin went into exile; a rustic gave him a clod, and in the end he returned to Jin. Your Majesty's dream—does the matter match this?"

units.zh: 蜀丞相诸葛亮问广汉秦密，董扶及任安所长。
units.en: Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang asked the Guanghan scholar Qin Mi what Dong Fu and Ren An respectively excelled at.
units.literal: The Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi of Guanghan what Dong Fu and Ren An were each good at.

units.zh: 放勛、重華之世，咸無意於受終，當塗、典午之君，雖有心於揖讓，皆以英才處萬乘，高勳御四海，故能大庇黔首，光宅區縣。
units.en: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.
units.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.

units.zh: 既而煙雲表色，日月呈瑞，緯聚東井，龍見譙邦，除舊布新，既彰玄象，遷虞事夏，且協謳訟，[2]九域八荒，同布衷款，百神群祀，皆有誠願。
units.en: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.
units.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.

units.zh: 梁氏以天祿斯改，期運永終，欽若唐、虞，推其鼎玉，朕東西退讓，拜手陳辭，避舜子於箕山之陽，求支伯於滄洲之野，而公卿敦逼，率土翹惶，天命難稽，遂享嘉祚。
units.en: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne.
units.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.

units.zh: 後主漸長大，愛宦人黃皓。
units.en: As Liu Shan matured he grew fond of the eunuch Huang Hao.
units.literal: The Later Lord gradually grew to adulthood; he favored the eunuch Huang Hao.

units.zh: 陳祗代允為侍中，與黃皓互相表裡，皓始預政事。
units.en: Chen Zhi succeeded Dong Yun as palace attendant and colluded openly with Huang Hao, who now entered politics.
units.literal: Chen Zhi replaced Yun as palace attendant; with Huang Hao they were mutual outer and inner [allies]; Hao began to participate in governance.

units.zh: 及鄧艾至蜀，聞皓奸險，收閉，將殺之，而皓厚賂艾左右，得免。
units.en: When Deng Ai entered Shu he jailed Huang Hao for villainy and meant to execute him, but Huang Hao bought off Deng Ai’s staff and walked free.
units.literal: When Deng Ai arrived in Shu, hearing Hao's treacherous cunning, he seized and imprisoned him and was about to kill him; but Hao richly bribed Ai's attendants and obtained release.

units.zh: 皓便闢佞慧，欲自容入。
units.en: Huang Hao used wit and flattery to worm his way inward.
units.literal: Hao then was clever at ingratiating flattery; he wished to insert himself by ingratiation.

units.zh: 終允之世，皓位不過黃門丞。
units.en: Throughout Dong Yun’s life Huang Hao never rose above assistant at the yellow gates.
units.literal: To the end of Yun's lifetime, Hao's rank did not exceed Assistant at the Yellow Gates.

units.zh: 祗死後，皓從黃門令為中常侍、奉車都尉，操弄威柄，終至覆國。
units.en: After Chen Zhi’s death Huang Hao rose from palace gate superintendent to household attendant and chief commandant for the imperial carriage, seized real power, and helped ruin the kingdom.
units.literal: After Zhi died, Hao went from Yellow Gates superintendent to Regular Palace Attendant and Chief Commandant for the Imperial Carriages; he wielded and toyed with authority until at last the state was overturned.

units.zh: 皓畏允，不敢為非。
units.en: Huang Hao feared Dong Yun too much to make open mischief.
units.literal: Hao feared Yun; he did not dare do wrong.

units.zh: 允常上則正色匡主，下則數責於皓。
units.en: Dong Yun rebuked the ruler to his face and scolded Huang Hao behind the scenes.
units.literal: Yun constantly upward then with stern countenance corrected the lord; downward he repeatedly reproached Hao.

units.zh: 和帝初立，議遣車騎將軍竇憲與征西將軍耿秉擊匈奴，恭上疏諫曰：
units.en: Early in Emperor He's reign the court debated dispatching Dou Xian and Geng Bing against the Xiongnu; Gong filed a memorial of opposition:
units.literal: When Emperor He had first been established, they debated sending General of Chariots and Cavalry Dou Xian and General Who Conquers the West Geng Bing to strike the Xiongnu; Gong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:

units.zh: 初，和帝末，下令麥秋得案驗薄刑，而州郡好以苛察為政，因此遂盛夏斷獄。
units.en: Late in Emperor He's reign the court allowed review of light sentences after the wheat harvest, yet local officials preferred harsh scrutiny and began holding criminal trials in the heat of summer.
units.literal: Formerly, near the end of Emperor He's reign, an order went out that at wheat harvest minor punishments might be investigated; but commanderies and provinces liked to govern by harsh scrutiny; therefore they consequently tried prison cases in midsummer.

units.zh: 和帝因朝會，召見諸儒，丕與侍中賈逵、尚書令黃香等相難數事，帝善丕說，罷朝，特賜冠幘履襪衣一襲。
units.en: At a formal audience Emperor He convened the scholars; Pi debated several points with Jia Kui and Huang Xiang—the emperor favored Pi's answers and at dismissal gifted him a full set of cap, headcloth, footwear, and robes.
units.literal: Emperor He, owing to court assembly, summoned audience with the various Confucians; Pi with Palace Attendant Jia Kui, Prefect of Masters of Writing Huang Xiang, and others mutually challenged on several matters; the emperor praised Pi's explanations; court dismissed; specially granted cap, turban, shoes, socks, one suit of clothes.

units.zh: 書奏，不從。
units.en: The emperor received the memorial and rejected it.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted; it was not followed.

units.zh: 十九年，進圍成都，璋蜀郡太守許靖將逾城降，事覺，不果。
units.en: In year 19 the army closed on Chengdu; Xu Jing, prefect of Shu under Liu Zhang, tried to slip over the wall to defect but was caught and could not complete it.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year they advanced to besiege Chengdu; Xu Jing, Liu Zhang’s Administrator of Shu Commandery, attempted to climb the walls and surrender but was discovered and failed.

units.zh: 正說曰：「天下有獲虛譽而無其實者，許靖是也。
units.en: Fa Zheng argued: “The world holds reputations without substance—Xu Jing is one.
units.literal: Zheng urged: “The realm has men who win empty fame without substance—Xu Jing is such.

units.zh: 然今主公始創大業，天下之人不可戶說，靖之浮稱，播流四海，若其不禮，天下之人以是謂主公為賤賢也。
units.en: Yet as you launch your rule you cannot lecture every home; Xu Jing’s renown rings everywhere—if you dishonor him, people will call you contemptuous of talent.
units.literal: Yet now you inaugurate a great enterprise; you cannot explain yourself household by household—Xu Jing’s inflated name circulates the realm—if you slight him, folk will say you scorn worthies.

units.zh: 先主於是乃厚待靖。
units.en: Liu Bei accordingly welcomed Xu Jing with honor.
units.literal: The Former Lord then treated Xu Jing generously.

units.zh: 靖處室則友於不穆，出身則受位非所，語信則夷險易心，論識則殆為釁首，安在其可寵先而有以感致者乎？
units.en: At home Xu Jing failed brotherly harmony; in career he took ill-fitting posts; in loyal speech he veered with fortune; in counsel he nearly sparked disaster—what merit earns awe?
units.literal: Xu Jing was no harmonious brother at home; in office he held posts unsuited to him; in speech he shifted heart between safety and peril; in judgment he nearly became the cause of strife—wherein lies favor that moves others?

units.zh: 璋以危亡在近，故不誅靖。
units.en: With collapse imminent Liu Zhang spared Xu Jing’s life.
units.literal: Because ruin pressed near, Liu Zhang did not execute Xu Jing.

units.zh: 璋既稽服，先主以此薄靖不用也。
units.en: Once Liu Zhang capitulated, Liu Bei despised Xu Jing and hesitated to use him.
units.literal: After Liu Zhang submitted, the Former Lord thought little of Xu Jing and would not employ him.

units.zh: 臣松之以為郭隗非賢，猶以權計蒙寵，況文休名聲夙著，天下謂之英偉，雖末年有瑕，而事不彰徹，若不加禮，何以釋遠近之惑乎？
units.en: Pei Songzhi answers: Guo Wei was mediocre yet duped a throne; Xu Jing’s name towered—ignore courtesy and you fuel rumor.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: Guo Wei was no sage yet won favor by stratagem—how much more Xu Jing, whose fame long marked him heroic among the realm; though flawed in old age the faults stayed hidden—without courtesy how quiet distant doubts?

units.zh: 至於友於不穆，失由子將，尋蔣濟之論，知非文休之尤。
units.en: Domestic discord traces to Xu Shao’s verdict—read Jiang Ji and Xu Jing’s guilt shrinks.
units.literal: As for unhappy brotherhood, blame falls on Zijiang—refer to Jiang Ji’s essay and see Xu Jing was hardly chief culprit.

units.zh: 文休為選官。
units.en: Xu Jing directed appointments.
units.literal: Xu Jing served as selection officer.

units.zh: 在卓未至之前，後遷中丞，不為超越。
units.en: That predated Zhuo’s arrival in Luoyang; his promotion to imperial secretary followed normal course.
units.literal: That was before Zhuo reached the capital; later he rose to Palace Assistant Clerk—no leap beyond merit.

units.zh: 非所，將謂仕於董卓。
units.en: implying he served Dong Zhuo.
units.literal: to mean serving Dong Zhuo.

units.zh: 卓初秉政，顯擢賢俊，受其策爵者森然皆是。
units.en: When Zhuo seized government he promoted talent widely—those who accepted titles were legion.
units.literal: When Zhuo first seized power he elevated worthies wholesale—those who took his patents filled the rolls.

units.zh: 法正以靖方隗，未為不當，而盛以封墓式閭為難，何其迂哉！
units.en: Fa Zheng’s analogy holds; Sun Sheng’s fuss over grave ritual is fussy pedantry.
units.literal: For Fa Zheng to pair Xu Jing with Guo Wei was not wrong—yet Sun Sheng treats tending tombs as scandal—how pedantic!

units.zh: 盛又譏其受
units.en: Sun Sheng also ridiculed Xu Jing’s acceptance of
units.literal: Sun Sheng further mocked his accepting

units.zh: 建興六年，亮出軍向祁山，時有宿將魏延、吳壹等，論者皆言以為宜令為先鋒，而亮違眾拔謖，統大眾在前，與魏將張郃戰於街亭，為郃所破，士卒離散。
units.en: In 228 Zhuge Liang struck toward Qishan. Everyone expected veterans such as Wei Yan or Wu Yi to lead the van, but he chose Ma Su instead. Ma Su took the main force forward, met Zhang He at Jieting, was shattered, and his men fled in disorder.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Jianxing, Liang led the army toward Qishan; at the time there were veteran generals Wei Yan, Wu Yi, and others; discussants all said they thought it right to order [them] to be vanguard, but Liang went against the multitude and elevated Su, commanding the great host in the van; he fought with Wei general Zhang He at Jieting; he was broken by He; officers and soldiers scattered and separated.

units.zh: 永元中，和帝追尊其母梁贵人曰恭怀皇后，陵曰西陵。
units.en: In Yongyuan, Hedi posthumously raised his mother, Lady Liang, to Empress Gonghuai; her tomb was Xiling.
units.literal: In the Yongyuan era Emperor He posthumously honored his mother, the Lady of Liang, as Empress Gonghuai, and her tomb was called Xiling.

units.zh: 以窦后配食章帝，恭怀后别就陵寝祭之。
units.en: Empress Dou shared Zhangdi’s cult, but Empress Gonghuai was worshipped separately at her tomb lodge.
units.literal: Empress Dou was paired to share Zhangdi’s offering, while Empress Gonghuai was separately worshipped at her mausoleum lodge.
